topic: Sharp pilot sizing for factorial rerandomization on a locally rich fixed-baseline domain. Condition on a deterministic complete baseline array known before assignment; all oracle-relevant uncertainty enters through a stable bounded conditional potential-outcome family whose global parameter set is the closure of a full-dimensional connected product of oracle and nuisance balls inside one regular identifiable chart. In a balanced two-wave 2^K factorial experiment, use complete randomization in an m-unit pilot, a pilot-measurable centered positive-support exact-alpha ellipsoidal rerandomization mixture in the main wave, and exact-inclusion pooled Horvitz-Thompson for the realized finite-population factorial vector. Relative to the matching full-n empirical raw-MSE oracle, prove the uniform second-order risk contrast A(beta)m/n^2+B(beta)/(nm)+o(m/n^2+1/(nm)), B=tr(Gamma I_eff^-1), and the global sharp envelope with unique m/sqrt(n) limit. Consumer: stable-batch replications of Menon et al.'s sequential factorial-cycle design with preregistered future baselines and continuously rich uncertainty. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The outcome-only likelihood, nuisance-efficient Gaussian boundary covariance, and exact pooled-HT contrast were derived. Every permitted single-wave HT risk is O(1/N). The global constant equals max over conv{(A,B)} of 2sqrt(AB), has a unique pilot fraction, and needs at most two active parameter values. Corrected disk information and exact rational enumeration verify acceptance 137/1000, minimum assignment probability 1/96, unequal inclusions 1/16 and 7/16, and zero HT bias. Baseline-leakage, finite-catalogue, endpoint, tie, lattice, and current-prior-art checks found no fatal defect in the final domain. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniformly that full-oracle gain minus weighted subset-oracle gain contributes A m/n^2 and empirical-oracle-centered finite HT action regret contributes B/(nm), with little-o remainder under exact ties, splitting, unequal inclusions, nuisance estimation, and arbitrary measurable actions. EARLY KILL TEST: On increasing cross-character arrays with m rounded from t sqrt(n), certify the scaled exact-HT contrast and localized action regret; any nonzero limiting lattice or unequal-inclusion correction not absorbed into A,B forces revision. open_problems.open_problem: What pilot size is uniformly second-order optimal for two-wave data-adaptive rerandomization in balanced 2^K factorial experiments when risk is measured against the matching full-sample empirical oracle?

source_refs.claim: The paper learns an oracle factorial-rerandomization criterion from a within-experiment subset and proves first-order oracle precision, but does not derive a sharp second-order pilot-size constant.
source_refs.author: Tingxuan Han and Ke Deng

source_refs.claim: For binary-arm two-wave experiments, conditional minimax regret is optimal up to constants and leads to an n^(2/3) worst-case pilot scale; it does not treat locally regular factorial rerandomization or a sharp empirical-oracle contrast.
source_refs.author: Juan C. Yamin

source_refs.claim: The two-stage procedure learns covariate importance from a pilot and establishes asymptotic efficiency, without optimizing pilot size against a full-n empirical oracle.
source_refs.author: Zhaoyang Liu, Tingxuan Han, Donald B. Rubin, and Ke Deng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The application paper advocates using earlier factorial cycles to design later cycles, but provides no design-based pilot-sizing or oracle-regret theory.
source_refs.author: Anil Menon, Sibu Chakrabarti, and Nadhamuni Nerella

open_problems.why_unsolved: Han and Deng establish first-order recovery for a learned factorial oracle, whereas sharp pilot sizing requires two uniform terms below first order: loss from withholding m units from the full-sample oracle and action regret from estimating its criterion. Yamin shows that global worst-case boundary behavior can instead produce an n^(2/3) scale, so obtaining a square-root scale requires exploiting the stated locally rich interior chart and proving that arbitrary pilot-measurable actions, nuisance estimation, unequal inclusions, and exact boundary randomization do not reintroduce the slower regime. Menon et al.'s sequential factorial-cycle workflow supplies the application need but no mathematical resolution.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform expansion R_n(m)-R_n^oracle=A(beta)m/n^2+B(beta)/(nm)+o(m/n^2+1/(nm)), followed by a sharp global-envelope theorem establishing the unique limit of m/sqrt(n).

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the closest factorial, finite-population problem in which a within-experiment subset learns an infeasible oracle rerandomization rule.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Multiple factorial effects create effect-specific balance priorities -> outcome relevance defines an infeasible oracle criterion -> a learning subset makes the criterion implementable -> allocating units between learning and final precision becomes the unresolved design problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine its sample-splitting representation and joint finite-population Gaussian approximation by retaining the oracle-loss and estimated-action terms through second order.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It has the same factorial-vector target and pilot-learned rerandomization architecture whose first-order equivalence must be sharpened.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its oracle-relative decision-loss decomposition and lower-bound comparison over all measurable pilot rules, replacing binary Neyman allocation by an ellipsoidal factorial-rerandomization action.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly separates pilot opportunity cost from noisy-action regret, while exposing the boundary phenomenon that the local product-ball assumptions must exclude.

open_problems.open_problem: Can pilot uncertainty about effect-specific covariate importance be converted into an exact-alpha, positive-support ellipsoidal rerandomization mixture that is locally asymptotically minimax over a full-dimensional oracle-and-nuisance product neighborhood?

source_refs.claim: The paper plugs pilot estimates of effect-specific covariate importance into an oracle factorial criterion and establishes first-order design-based validity, leaving local uncertainty in the learned criterion unresolved.
source_refs.author: Tingxuan Han and Ke Deng

source_refs.claim: The Bayesian criterion averages asymptotic variance over uncertainty about covariate importance, but does not derive a nuisance-efficient local minimax boundary for factorial effects.
source_refs.author: Zhaoyang Liu, Tingxuan Han, Donald B. Rubin, and Ke Deng
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper derives efficiency bounds across covariate- and history-adaptive experiments in a sequential superpopulation setting, not under exact-alpha finite-population rerandomization.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong

open_problems.why_unsolved: A consistent plug-in ellipsoid suffices for first-order oracle equivalence, but near a boundary between competing oracle geometries the pilot's nuisance-efficient covariance determines which assignments should receive acceptance mass. Pointwise Slutsky arguments do not determine a locally minimax randomized action. The first proof step that changes is the replacement of plug-in consistency by a joint local asymptotic experiment for oracle and nuisance coordinates, after which one must optimize while preserving exact acceptance probability and strictly positive assignment support.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A locally asymptotically minimax characterization of the pilot-measurable ellipsoidal mixture, with its boundary law expressed through I_eff^(-1) and an explicit regret constant B=tr(Gamma I_eff^(-1)).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation proceeds from heterogeneous factorial priorities to a learned oracle criterion, matching the destination problem closely.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Covariates matter differently for different factorial effects -> an oracle importance matrix selects the balance geometry -> a pilot estimates that matrix with non-negligible local uncertainty -> a covariance-aware randomized design is needed near oracle boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over its optimization of uncertainty-integrated asymptotic variance over acceptance regions, replacing a fixed prior by the nuisance-efficient Gaussian law of the pilot.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems choose rerandomization geometry under uncertainty about outcome-covariate relevance; the target adds factorial-vector weights and local frequentist minimaxity.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its tangent-space and efficiency-bound comparison for adaptive experimental designs to isolate the efficient information for the pilot's oracle-relevant parameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired trace constant is an efficiency calculation for a learned causal-design action, with finite-population assignment and exact-alpha constraints replacing sequential superpopulation sampling.

open_problems.open_problem: Does exact-inclusion pooled Horvitz-Thompson estimation admit a uniform second-order factorial-vector risk expansion when a pilot-learned rerandomization mixture induces unequal treatment-combination inclusion probabilities?

source_refs.claim: Its finite-sample unbiasedness result for ordinary factorial estimators relies on symmetry of the rerandomization acceptance criterion.
source_refs.author: Zach Branson, Tirthankar Dasgupta, and Donald B. Rubin

source_refs.claim: The paper supplies exactly unbiased inverse-inclusion estimators and joint-inclusion variance identities for unequal-probability sampling.
source_refs.author: D. G. Horvitz and D. J. Thompson
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: General Horvitz-Thompson theory establishes quadratic-mean consistency under broad experimental designs, but not a pilot-conditional second-order factorial risk expansion.
source_refs.author: Angèle Delevoye and Fredrik Sävje
source_refs.venue: Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference

open_problems.why_unsolved: Classical factorial rerandomization uses sign-symmetric acceptance rules and ordinary difference-in-means estimators. A pilot-measurable mixture with randomized tie splitting can retain positive support while producing unequal unit-by-treatment inclusion probabilities, so the symmetry argument no longer applies. Exact Horvitz-Thompson weights repair the conditional first moment, but existing general HT theory does not propagate random pilot-generated first- and second-order inclusion probabilities through the pooled two-wave factorial-vector MSE at the 1/(nm) scale. The first missing step is an exact conditional representation of joint inclusion probabilities for the learned mixture.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact conditional unbiasedness result plus a uniform covariance and raw-MSE expansion for the pooled factorial Horvitz-Thompson vector under unequal inclusions, pilot/main dependence, and randomized ties.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest destination architecture: pilot learning followed by rerandomization for the complete factorial-effect vector.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Outcome-informed rerandomization improves factorial precision -> pilot adaptation changes the realized assignment law -> pooling both waves requires their exact inclusion probabilities -> design-based HT risk must be analyzed under the learned unequal-probability law.

method_exemplars.technique: Use exact first-order inclusion weights for factorial totals and the joint-inclusion covariance identity as the algebraic basis of the pooled risk calculation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The learned mixture is a finite unequal-probability design, precisely the structure for which Horvitz-Thompson identities remove first-moment selection bias.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the finite-population random-partition CLT for multiple treatments and vector outcomes after rewriting the weighted factorial estimator using exact inclusion indicators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is a joint finite-population causal contrast with multiple treatment combinations, but its partition probabilities are pilot-dependent and nonuniform.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a uniform conditional second-order expansion for factorial Horvitz-Thompson risk under exact-alpha ellipsoidal rerandomization that either eliminates or explicitly identifies lattice and tie-boundary corrections?

source_refs.claim: The paper develops finite-population Gaussian and Berry-Esseen control for best-choice Mahalanobis rerandomization, yielding large-sample inference rather than a conditional second-order risk expansion.
source_refs.author: Yuhao Wang and Xinran Li

source_refs.claim: The finite-population CLT covers multiple treatments, factors, and vector outcomes but not tie-uniform conditioning on a discrete, pilot-estimated ellipsoidal event.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li and Peng Ding
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: The paper derives truncated-Gaussian first-order limits and conservative confidence regions for factorial effects under fixed symmetric convex acceptance rules.
source_refs.author: Xinran Li, Peng Ding, and Donald B. Rubin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing rerandomization theory replaces a discrete randomization distribution by a Gaussian vector conditioned on a fixed ellipsoid. That suffices for first-order covariance, but with m of order sqrt(n), the 1/(nm) action-regret term lies at a scale where discontinuous exact-alpha boundary selection, repeated imbalance scores, and lattice structure can matter. An unconditional Berry-Esseen bound does not by itself control expectations after conditioning on a random pilot-estimated boundary. The Gaussian-conditioning step must be replaced by a local-limit or smoothing argument that tracks boundary mass and randomized tie splitting uniformly over deterministic baseline arrays.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform conditional Edgeworth or local-limit expansion for exact Horvitz-Thompson risk through the learned ellipsoidal boundary, proving lattice and tie corrections are o(m/n^2+1/(nm)) or displaying the additional correction term.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates quantitative approximation by showing how finite-population Gaussian error bounds support inference for a highly selective rerandomization rule.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: More selective assignment rules improve covariate balance -> conditioning can magnify Gaussian-approximation error -> quantitative Berry-Esseen control restores first-order inference -> sharp pilot optimization requires boundary- and lattice-sensitive second-order control.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine its finite-population Berry-Esseen comparison and conditioning-probability bounds for quadratic risk functionals and randomized exact-alpha boundary events.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest quantitative approximation for a rerandomization law whose selection event amplifies small distributional errors.

method_exemplars.technique: Start from its random-partition representation of multivariate factorial statistics and add a second-order combinatorial expansion uniform over deterministic finite populations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination statistic is a multivariate finite-population causal contrast whose randomness comes solely from assignment, exactly the regime covered there at first order.

literature_map:
Morgan and Rubin (2012, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1207.5625) formalize fixed-threshold Mahalanobis rerandomization and its variance gain.
Branson, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2016, Annals of Applied Statistics, arXiv:1511.01973) extend rerandomization to 2^K factorial effects; ordinary-estimator unbiasedness relies on symmetric acceptance.
Li, Ding, and Rubin (2018, PNAS, arXiv:1604.00698) derive the treatment-control truncated-Gaussian randomization limit.
Zhou, Ernst, Morgan, Rubin, and Zhang (2018, Biometrika, arXiv:1706.04182) analyze sequentially enrolled batches, emphasizing balance, randomness, and computation rather than pilot sizing.
Li, Ding, and Rubin (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1812.10911) establish joint factorial-effect limits, peakedness, and conservative confidence regions under fixed rerandomization rules.
Li and Ding (2020, JRSSB, arXiv:1906.11291) combine rerandomization with regression adjustment and distinguish design precision from estimated precision.
Liu, Han, Rubin, and Deng (2025, JASA, arXiv:2303.07904) optimize an outcome-informed Bayesian acceptance criterion and give a two-stage treatment-control implementation.
Han and Deng (2026, arXiv:2609.02078) provide the closest anchor: within-sample learning of an oracle criterion for the full 2^K factorial vector.
Their first-order theory recovers oracle precision but does not supply a uniform second-order pilot-allocation constant or exact unequal-inclusion HT expansion.
Yamin (2026, arXiv:2607.16982) shows that finite pilots can make feasible Neyman allocation arbitrarily poor and derives conditional minimax-regret rates; its global boundary regime yields an n^(2/3) pilot scale rather than the proposed local square-root scale.
Branson, Li, and Ding (2024, Biometrika, arXiv:2201.02486) derive power and total-sample-size formulas for fixed rerandomization, not allocation between learning and deployment.
Schindl and Branson (2024, arXiv:2403.12815) characterize quadratic-form rerandomization and minimax Euclidean geometry without pilot estimation or factorial-vector regret.
Kallus (2018, JRSSB, DOI:10.1111/rssb.12240) and Kallus (2021, JRSSB, arXiv:2005.03151) expose the tension between optimal precision and sufficient randomization for design-based inference.
Wang and Li (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2312.02513) add Berry-Esseen control for best-choice rerandomization, but the scanned literature contains no conditional second-order expansion uniform over exact ties and lattice baselines.
Menon, Chakrabarti, and Nerella (2002, Pharmaceutical Development and Technology, DOI:10.1081/PDT-120002228) motivate iterative factorial cycles in product development; Horvitz and Thompson (1952) and Delevoye and Sävje (2020) cover unequal-probability unbiasedness and consistency, not pooled two-wave factorial oracle regret.
